content: A Nabothian cyst is a mucus-filled lump that forms on the surface of the cervix. Each Nabothian cyst appears as a small, white, raised bump. There may be more than one cyst present. The cervix contains glands and cells that produce mucus. Sometimes, these glands can become covered by a type of skin cell called squamous epithelium. When this occurs, the mucus secretions accumulate within the blocked glands, leading to the formation of a smooth, rounded bump on the cervix. This bump is referred to as a Nabothian cyst. This condition is typically identified during a routine pelvic examination. During a pelvic exam, a physician may observe a small, smooth, rounded lump (or multiple lumps) on the surface of the cervix. In rare cases, a colposcopy may be performed to differentiate Nabothian cysts from other types of bumps or lesions that can occur on the cervix. Occasionally, the cyst may be opened to confirm its diagnosis as a Nabothian cyst. Treatment is generally not required for Nabothian cysts, as they do not cause any medical issues. In rare instances, if the cysts are large enough to alter the shape of the cervical canal and make examinations more challenging, they may be opened and drained. Nabothian cysts are harmless and represent a benign condition. In rare cases, the cysts may become so numerous or enlarged that they cause the cervix to become enlarged or obstructed, which can make it difficult to perform a Pap smear. There is no known method to prevent the formation of Nabothian cysts.
